To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the jet power exceeds the accretion power for rapidly spinning black holes accreting in a magnetically arrested state, that the jet power is proportional to the black hole mass and to the square of the black hole spin, and that the power in the jet and wind together is proportional to the accretion rate and to the magnetic flux at infinity.
(1) for a rapidly spinning black-hole magnetosphere, the jet power is much larger than the total accretion power, and (2) for a slowly spinning black-hole magnetar, the wind power is much larger.

(i) the jet power is much larger than the total rate of mass energy accretion onto the black hole and (ii) the jet power depends on black hole spin in a manner that is qualitatively similar to the Eddington limit for thin discs, but with the jet power being much larger than the Eddington luminosity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of magnetic fields in accretion discs.
the physics of accretion flows in the strong gravity regime around black holes.
the physics of accretion discs and jets around black holes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the jet has a small feedback effect on its local environment, the wind is likely to have a significant effect on its host galaxy and beyond.
, in the case of radiatively inefficient thick accretion disc systems, feedback on large scales is dominated by the wind, whereas on small scales it is dominated by the jet.
the jet is the dominant source of feedback on scales larger than the jet radius, while the wind is the dominant source on smaller scales.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the jet is the main energy output from a rapidly spinning thick accretion disc, but the wind provides the most effective feedback.

the jet is a powerful and efficient engine for extracting rotational energy from the black hole, but it has a small opening angle and is unlikely to provide strong feedback on its immediate surroundings, while the wind has a wide opening angle and is likely to be the primary agent for feedback.
the jet is a powerful but narrowly directed outflow, while the wind is a more modest but wide-angle outflow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wind is likely to play the most important role in regulating black hole growth and in shaping the host galaxy.
the energy and momentum output of a radiatively inefficient accreting black hole can be estimated from the black hole mass, spin and the magnetic flux threading the horizon.
the jet is likely to be the dominant energy source for feedback in the magnetically dominated regime, while the wind is likely to be more important when the disc is not strongly magnetized.
